frontmatter.name: npc_decision
frontmatter.description: System message for an LLM-driven NPC's ReAct decision (text_adventure_games/npc.py, LLMAgent). Renders the persona and goals, and -- on the free-text path -- the labeled Reasoning/Action/Duration instruction. The structured tool-calling path renders the same persona/goals block but omits the instruction, because there the tool schema is the output contract. The character's name is deliberately left out: identity rides on the first-person persona, and the observation already names the scene and everyone in it, so the model speaks as "I" without being told its own name.

persona.description: First-person persona string. The Persona line is dropped when empty.

goals_block.description: Pre-formatted goals grouped by tier (see LLMAgent._format_goals). The Goals section is dropped when empty.

include_instruction.description: True on the free-text path (append the ReAct instruction); False on the structured tool-calling path (omit it).

reasoning_label.description: The reasoning line label, e.g. "Reasoning:" (from ReActLabel).

action_label.description: The action line label, e.g. "Action:" (from ReActLabel).

duration_label.description: The duration line label, e.g. "Duration:" (from ReActLabel).

sample.persona: I am the troll. I guard the drawbridge.
sample.goals_block:
Short-term:
  - keep the player off the bridge

decide.rendered:
You are an NPC in a text adventure game.
Persona: I am the troll. I guard the drawbridge.
Goals:
Short-term:
  - keep the player off the bridge
Based on your persona, goals, and the current situation, choose a single game command to execute. Reply with exactly three lines:
Reasoning: <one short sentence explaining your choice>
Action: <the command, e.g. 'attack player', 'go north', 'take sword'>
Duration: <estimated in-game minutes this action takes, e.g. 5>
If no available command can accomplish what you need, your Action may be: propose <what you need> because <why> — this records your request for the world's designers.

frontmatter.name: match_intent
frontmatter.description: Parser system instructions for matching a user's input to the closest known action (LlmParser.determine_intent's LLM fallback). The numbered list of command descriptions is appended by LlmParser._pick_option. For agent-driven actors (#621) allow_none adds the licensing sentence for the "none of these commands fit the input" decline option the parser appends to that list.

allow_none.description: True when the option list carries the decline option (agent-driven actors); adds the sentence licensing the model to pick it. Defaults falsy: the human-player rendering is byte-identical to the pre-#621 one.
